coverage_caveat: 2020-2024 covers only bills that received a floor roll call (plus HB2 budget trailers); committee- and voice-vote deaths in those years are not in the set. 2025-2026 coverage is complete from the official database. Cross-year failure-rate comparisons are unsafe; within-year and topic patterns are reliable.

theme_scorecards.theme: Building more homes: zoning and land use
theme_scorecards.note: Every enactment is from 2025-2026: homes in commercial zones (HB631 2025, HB1010 2026, HB1588 2026), limits on local dwelling-unit restrictions (HB457 2025), plus the 2021 planning omnibus SB86. The repeal attempts against these new laws (HB1011, HB1012, HB1016 in 2026) all died.

The sweeping version (two ADUs per lot by right, HB1291 2024) passed the House 220-143 and was killed in the Senate. Narrower wins followed: HB577 (2025) broadened the ADU definition including detached ADUs, and HB1079 (2026) allowed ADUs in non-conforming structures. ADU finance bills (HB604, HB1662) died.

Standalone money bills usually die - often after unanimous Senate votes - while the same dollars move through HB2, the budget trailer: Affordable Housing Fund ($25M in 2021 and again in 2023), InvestNH, Housing Champion ($5M), Partners in Housing. New taxes for housing (HB1786, HB1707) and transfer-tax increases (HB530, SB81) never reached a floor win.

Application-fee limits, rent registries, algorithm bans, pet-fee rules, mold remediation, and municipal rental regulation all died, most in the House. What passed is narrow: optional electronic rent payment (HB309 2025) and an EV-charging study for renters (HB111 2023).

Voucher-discrimination bans died three times (2022, 2023, 2025). Notice-before-sale died three times (2023, 2025, and the 2022 voucher companion). What passed is procedural: the landlord-tenant court omnibus (SB126 2021) and eviction notice/process updates (HB1598 2026). The 2020 COVID eviction pause was vetoed; the override failed.

Standalone shelter-funding bills died at Senate deadlines or on tables (SB415 2022, SB113/SB114 2025, HB519); the big shelter dollars moved through HB2 ($10M in 2023; $10M opioid-fund shelter money in 2025). The Council on Housing Stability was codified (HB503, enacted 2022) and updated (SB179 2025).

Resident protections advanced narrowly (SB166 2025 sale notice) and tiny houses/yurts were legalized as innovative housing (HB1681 2026). But the dispute-resolution Board of Manufactured Housing was repealed by HB2 2023 while the bill to fix it (SB203) died between the chambers, and by-right manufactured housing (HB685 2025) died in conference.

theme_scorecards.theme: Land use boards, appeals, and the courts
theme_scorecards.note: Conflict-of-interest recusal (HB92 2025) and abutter-appeal rules (HB1359 2024) became law; board training died repeatedly (2020 HB1629, 2021 HB586, 2022 SB400, 2026 HB1802). The Housing Appeals Board was restructured through HB2 2025, not a standalone bill.

Study vehicles pass more easily (zoning enabling act commission HB399 2025, housing investment trust study HB633 2025), and the Senate routed several 2026 housing bills to interim study. A 10-year strategic housing plan (HB1814) stayed on the House table.

topic_reality_cards.topic: Letting homes be built in commercial zones
topic_reality_cards.what_happened: This is the record's clearest recent success. HB631 (2025) permitted residential building in commercial zoning - the House rejected a motion to kill it 128-211 - and became law. HB1010 (2026) extended multi-family residential development on commercially zoned land and became law (Chapter 319). HB1588 (2026) packaged multifamily-in-commercial-districts with parking-mandate limits and housing infrastructure grant money and passed a conference report 185-171. Broader versions (HB1065, SB90 - high-density residential on commercial land) still died.
topic_reality_cards.chokepoint: None for the moderate versions since 2025; the aggressive density versions die on the House or Senate floor.
topic_reality_cards.who_carried: Cross-party House coalitions; 78 House Republicans joined most Democrats to keep HB631 alive.
open_questions: How many homes the new commercial-zone laws actually produce (first data due via municipal reporting)
Whether 2027 sees repeal attempts like 2026's HB1011/HB1016

topic_reality_cards.what_happened: The big statewide mandate - two ADUs per lot by right (HB1291, 2024) - passed the House 220-143 (150 of 181 Democrats and 67 Republicans voting yes) and was killed in the Senate, which indefinitely postponed it after a rescue amendment failed 8-16. The next two years produced narrower wins: HB577 (2025) broadened the ADU definition including detached units and became law (Chapter 197); HB1079 (2026) let ADUs go into non-conforming structures (Chapter 210). A 2026 attempt to repeal the ADU statutes outright (HB1012) died, ADU loan guarantees (HB1662) and ADU parking relief (HB1006) also died, while ADU loan forgiveness (HB604) went to interim study.
topic_reality_cards.chokepoint: The Senate floor for broad mandates; House committees for finance add-ons.
topic_reality_cards.who_carried: Cross-party House majorities; Senate Democrats offered the failed 2024 rescue amendment.
topic_reality_cards.venue: State legislature sets the statewide ADU floor (RSA 674); towns regulate above it.
open_questions: Whether ADU production data (HB1625's failed reporting idea) emerges another way
Whether a Senate-palatable version of the two-ADU mandate exists

topic_reality_cards.topic: Streamlining local zoning procedures for housing
topic_reality_cards.what_happened: The same idea has now failed three ways in three years: SB538 (2024) passed the Senate and was killed on the House floor 188-173; SB84 (2025-2026) passed the Senate 13-10, was carried across the biennium, and ended in interim study; the House's own vehicles (HB1008, HB1713) died in committee or on the floor in 2026. What has passed instead is targeted: HB457 (2025) limiting specific local dwelling-unit restrictions.
topic_reality_cards.chokepoint: The House floor and House Housing committee.
topic_reality_cards.who_carried: Senate Republicans (Sen. Keith Murphy prime-sponsored SB84) with split House votes.
topic_reality_cards.venue: State legislature (RSA 674-676 preemption of local process).
open_questions: What the interim study on SB84 recommends for 2027
Whether procedure bills fare differently if split into single-subject pieces

topic_reality_cards.topic: Putting state money into the Affordable Housing Fund
topic_reality_cards.what_happened: The dollars are real but they never arrive by standalone bill. SB152 (2021) passed the Senate 24-0 and the House killed it - while the 2021 budget trailer (HB2, 91:376) carried $25 million for the fund. HB2 2023 (79:43) carried another $25 million. The standalone attempts to make funding automatic - raising the real estate transfer tax share (HB530, SB81 2025) - died at Senate deadlines, and SB419 (2026, Housing Champion plus fund appropriations) went to interim study 16-8. New dedicated taxes for housing (HB1786 luxury second homes; HB1707 vacancy tax) died on or before the House floor.
topic_reality_cards.chokepoint: Standalone: the second chamber or the Senate deadline. Via HB2: none - it has passed every cycle.
topic_reality_cards.who_carried: Senate sponsors of both parties (SB152 was Sen. Gray, R); budget writers deliver the money.
topic_reality_cards.venue: State legislature, in practice through the biennial budget.
open_questions: Whether fund appropriations continue in the 2027 budget
What happens to InvestNH/Housing Champion balances as federal money winds down

topic_reality_cards.topic: Rewarding towns that welcome housing (Housing Champion / InvestNH / Partners in Housing)
topic_reality_cards.what_happened: The incentive-program family is the record's steadiest thread - and it lives in HB2. SB145 (2023) passed the Senate 21-3 and its Housing Champion program was enacted through HB2 2023 (79:462-466, $5M). HB2 2025 extended the money (141:355) and added Partners in Housing for workforce housing on public land (141:212) - after the standalone version (HB572) had been killed on the House floor 191-156. A 2026 repeal of Housing Champion (HB1196) passed the House 185-166 on near-party lines (Republicans yes) and was killed by the Senate. The business-loan variant (SB279 2025) died at the Senate deadline.
topic_reality_cards.chokepoint: Standalone bills die in the House; the programs survive inside the budget and survived a repeal attempt.
topic_reality_cards.who_carried: Senate sponsors across parties (SB145: Sen. Perkins Kwoka, D); House Republicans led the repeal.
topic_reality_cards.venue: State legislature via the budget; municipalities opt in voluntarily.
open_questions: Whether repeal returns in 2027
How many municipalities win designation and build

topic_reality_cards.topic: Banning discrimination against tenants with housing vouchers
topic_reality_cards.what_happened: Filed three times, dead three times, each earlier than the last: 2022's HB1291 was tabled on the House floor 179-148 after an 11-10 committee split; 2023's HB469 was killed by voice vote after the tabling pattern; 2025's HB628 died in the House. No version has ever passed either chamber.
open_questions: Whether a narrower version (e.g. veterans' vouchers) changes the vote
What share of NH landlords accept vouchers today

topic_reality_cards.topic: Regulating rents, fees, and rental practices
topic_reality_cards.what_happened: Nothing that touches the price of renting has passed. Municipal rental regulation authority (HB95 2023) was crushed 301-63. Rent-increase notice (HB567 2023) lost on the House floor. The rent registry + algorithm ban (HB558 2025), the application-fee ban (HB1371 2026), the one-fee-per-year cap (HB1375 2026), the price-fixing-software ban (HB1612 2026), pet-fee rules (HB1553 2026), and rental mold remediation (HB1143 2026) all died in the House. The exceptions run the other way or are narrow: HB309 (2025) made electronic rent payment optional, and HB1336 (2026) - loosening the security-deposit cap - passed both chambers and was vetoed.
topic_reality_cards.chokepoint: The House, usually its Housing or Judiciary committees and the floor.
topic_reality_cards.who_carried: House Democrats on tenant-cost bills; Republicans on the deposit-cap exception.
topic_reality_cards.venue: State legislature; NH has no local rent regulation authority to begin with.
open_questions: Whether the HB1336 veto is overridden this fall
Whether fee-transparency (rather than fee-limit) framing changes outcomes

topic_reality_cards.what_happened: Procedural updates pass; substantive protections do not. SB126 (2021), an omnibus rewrite of landlord-tenant proceedings, passed the Senate 24-0 and became law (Chapter 152); HB1598 (2026) updated eviction notice and court process (Chapter 308). But 60-day notice for at-will evictions (HB351 2025), renovation-eviction limits (HB401 2023, lost 154-213), notice before a building is sold (HB112 2023, HB444 2025), and Social Security disruption safeguards (HB1171 2026, killed 186-155) all died in the House. The landlord-side expansion of eviction grounds (HB1499 2026) passed the House 193-154 and died in conference. The 2020 COVID eviction/foreclosure pause (HB1247) passed both chambers and was vetoed; the override failed 187-148.
topic_reality_cards.chokepoint: The House floor for tenant-side bills; conference for landlord-side.
topic_reality_cards.who_carried: Democrats on tenant-side bills; Republicans on HB1499.
open_questions: Whether notice-before-sale returns for a fourth try
How the new HB1598 process changes eviction case outcomes

topic_reality_cards.what_happened: Standalone shelter funding has never passed in this record: SB415 (2022, shelter rates) was tabled 13-11 in the Senate; SB113 and SB114 (2025) passed unanimous or near-unanimous Senate votes and then died at the Senate's own end-of-year deadline; HB519 (Waypoint youth shelter) died in the House. The money that did arrive came through HB2: $8M for shelter rates plus $2M for cold-weather capacity in 2023, and $5M a year of opioid-settlement money for year-round emergency shelter in 2025. The Council on Housing Stability was codified by HB503 (enacted 2022) and updated by SB179 (2025).
topic_reality_cards.chokepoint: Standalone: Senate Finance and the calendar. Via HB2: none.
topic_reality_cards.who_carried: Senate Democrats (SB415: Sen. Kahn) and bipartisan sponsors on councils.
topic_reality_cards.venue: State legislature via the budget; DHHS administers.
open_questions: What happens when opioid-fund shelter money ends in 2027
Whether shelter rates keep pace with reported per-bed costs

topic_reality_cards.topic: Manufactured homes, tiny homes, and their residents
topic_reality_cards.what_happened: Two narrow wins: SB166 (2025) requires notice before a manufactured home in a resident-owned community is sold, and HB1681 (2026) legalized tiny houses and yurts as innovative housing (House concurrence 242-102). The losses are structural: HB2 2023 (79:301) repealed the Board of Manufactured Housing - the dispute forum for park residents - while SB203, which would have restructured it, died between the chambers; SB318 (2024) on the installation-standards board was vetoed; by-right manufactured housing in residential zones (HB685 2025) died in conference; and 2026 bills to weaken manufactured-housing requirements (HB1016) also died.
topic_reality_cards.chokepoint: Conference committees and the governor; the board repeal happened inside the budget trailer.
topic_reality_cards.who_carried: Mixed sponsors; resident-protection bills largely from Democrats, deregulation from Republicans.
topic_reality_cards.venue: State legislature (RSA 205-A); the board's functions now sit with the courts/OPLC.
open_questions: Where park residents take disputes now that the board is gone
Whether by-right manufactured housing returns

deliberation_prompts: Standalone housing-money bills die while the same dollars pass inside HB2. If an idea needs state money, what does that pattern suggest about timing it to a budget year?
The two-ADU mandate passed the House with 220 votes and died in the Senate. Is the obstacle the idea, or its scope - and what did the narrower ADU laws that passed leave out?
Tenant-cost bills (fees, notice, vouchers) have stopped on the House floor in every recent session. What would have to change for one to reach the Senate?
The Legislature keeps choosing incentives for willing towns (Housing Champion, Partners in Housing) over mandates on all towns. Which trade-offs matter most to your group?
Five 2025 Senate housing bills died at the Senate's own end-of-year deadline, several after unanimous votes. Is that a 'no' on the ideas, or a calendar problem?
The Board of Manufactured Housing was repealed inside a 600-section budget bill while the standalone fix died. How should groups track housing policy that moves inside HB2?
Three housing vetoes in six years, with one override pending. When a proposal passes both chambers on party-line votes, what does the record say happens next?
The 2026 session killed 51 housing bills and sent 11 to interim study. Which of those studies are worth following into 2027?
